Consult Summary:
- 42-year-old woman, 4 weeks post–cesarean section, with acute onset shortness of breath for ~1 hour; clinician concerned for possible postpartum thromboembolism and advised urgent hospital assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: sudden shortness of breath beginning while sitting watching TV, started within the last hour.
- Associated symptoms: new cough beginning yesterday; sensation of heart "really going" (palpitations).
- Chest symptoms: no chest pain at rest; chest feels sore on deep inspiration and the chest/C-section scar are tender.
- Onset/duration/progression: cough began yesterday; shortness of breath started acutely in the past hour and was not previously experienced.
- Pertinent negatives: no sputum production reported; no prior similar shortness of breath episodes noted; baby has no cough/cold.
- Past medical/obstetric history: recent cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Medications: codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented; reported taken fairly regularly after C-section but likely not taken for ~1 week.
- Allergies: ibuprofen — reaction not documented.
- Family history: mother has had leg clots previously.
- Social / caregiving: currently with newborn; partner at work; patient will travel to hospital with baby.

Examination:
- Vitals: none formally recorded.
- Examination findings: patient palpated her radial pulse and reported counting 30 beats during a timed count; clinician interpreted this as a slightly fast heart rate. C-section scar and chest described as tender by patient.

Impression:
- Acute shortness of breath in the postpartum period with new cough and palpitations; clinician concerned about possible thromboembolic event (e.g., pulmonary embolism) given recent C-section.

Plan:
- Urgent hospital evaluation recommended for further assessment (imaging and treatment as indicated).
- Patient declined ambulance and elected to go to hospital herself with the baby; advised to go promptly and bring items for the baby.
- Advised to withhold codeine for the time being prior to hospital assessment.
- Counseling provided that if a clot is confirmed, anticoagulant treatment can be given (per clinician discussion).
- No additional tests or follow-up appointments were specified in the transcript.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but expected elements: formal vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation), focused respiratory and cardiovascular exam, details of codeine dose/route/frequency and last dose timing, smoking status, full medication list, bleeding risk/anticoagulation history, breastfeeding status, leg symptoms (for DVT) and leg examination, obstetric details beyond C-section (e.g., perioperative complications).
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality: audible and clear; minimal interruptions, clinically sufficient for assessment.
